movie_title: S$33m support package to help social residential homes transit to new licensing framework
tags: Ministry of Social and Family Development
introduction: Singapore has passed new laws to enhance the quality of care at social residential homes. A S$33 mil
lead_intro: Learn about the new regulations and licensing framework in Singapore aimed at improving the quality of care in social residential homes.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of the $33 million set aside by Singapore?
choices: To help social residential home operators improve care standards
quiz.answer: To help social residential home operators improve care standards
quiz.explanation: The $33 million is intended to assist social residential home operators in raising their standard of care services and improving residents' welfare.

quiz.question: What will the new licensing framework in Singapore focus on?
choices: Enhancing the quality of care at social residential homes
quiz.answer: Enhancing the quality of care at social residential homes
quiz.explanation: The new laws aim to enhance the quality of care at social residential homes through a new licensing framework.

quiz.question: What type of checks will be mandatory for full-time staff at social residential homes in Singapore?
quiz.explanation: The new laws will make background checks compulsory for all full-time staff at social residential homes.

quiz.question: What is a measure that will be implemented to ensure high standards among social residential home operators?
choices: Unannounced inspections by an independent board of visitors
quiz.answer: Unannounced inspections by an independent board of visitors
quiz.explanation: Unannounced visits by an independent board of visitors across all homes will be conducted to ensure and maintain standards of care.

quiz.question: What penalties will be imposed for unauthorized operation of a home under the new regulations?
quiz.explanation: The unauthorized operation of a home will be subject to a $100,000 fine, a significant increase from the current $5,000 fine.
